mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.4 percentage points for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained above-0.4pp monthly UNRATE increases.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO and a fall in HOUST by more than 2% month-over-month signals supply chain bottling with reduced housing availability, which raises input costs and reduces consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month + 1% AND HOUST < previous month - 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO rises and HOUST falls by the specified amounts.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in PAYEMS for two consecutive months indicates weakening employment and consumer spending power, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative following two consecutive monthly PAYEMS declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a surge in household savings, which typically precedes a reduction in consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is persistently above its 12-month moving average for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both UNRATE and PAYEMS above their 6-month averages signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both UNRATE and PAYEMS exceed their 6-month averages.
